newsitem.title: ITALY: MTV signs deal with Italy's Rete A.
newsitem.headline: MTV signs deal with Italy's Rete A.

text.p: U.S. music and youth entertainment network MTV signed a deal with Italian terrestrial TV station RETE A allowing it to broadcast to more than 12 million households throughout Italy.
A statement issued by the U.S. company said MTV Networks Europe would be able to broadcast in Italy throughout the day and night from September 1, 1997.
The deal was part of a European strategy to increase MTV's appeal to viewers by tailoring its schedule, programme content and play list to the tastes of viewers throughout Europe.
Digital technology had allowed MTV to create customised MTV services for Northern, Central and Southern Europe and a dedicated service for Britain was planned for later in 1997.
MTV President and CEO Brent Hansen said the deal would "dramatically increase MTV's presence in Italy ... This agreement is key to the continued development of MTV's regional expansion in Europe."
MTV said it appointed Antonio Campo Dall'Orto as Managing Director MTV Networks Europe (Southern), based in Milan. Dall'Orto was recruited from Italian broadcaster Canale Cinque.
MTV Networks Europe is wholly owned by Viacom Inc in the United States.
